correctness.rationale: The residual q=1-(1-z)Q ranges exactly over quadratics q(1)=1. Strict convexity and two isometric involutions force the real palindromic form. A one-dimensional strictly convex minimization gives 0<u_p<1/2 and Q_p=(1+t_p+z)/(2+t_p). The arcsine stationarity function D_p is strictly increasing for every finite real p>1, negative at zero and positive at infinity. Uniform endpoint Laplace estimates have respective prefactors q^(-3/2)/(2 sqrt(2pi)) and 2q^(-1/2)/sqrt(2pi), with q=p-1, so the balance ratio is ((2+t)/(2-t))^q/(4q) and q t_p=log(4q)+o(1). Boundary conditions, gamma constants, and normalization are written explicitly in RESULT.md. Finite level p=2,4 and high-p numerical roots were reproduced using the attached checker; finite tests do not prove the limit.

value.rationale: Centner (2022), immediately after tabulating precisely this generator, explicitly asks whether the degree-one roots converge as the Hardy exponent grows. This theorem answers that concrete source-motivated problem for f=1-z for all real p>1, determines the limiting boundary point and the nontrivial sharp logarithmic margin, and explains it by competing arcsine endpoint saddles with different q power laws. That margin quantifies loss of zero separation/stability of the simplest noninvertible boundary-zero inverse filter, rather than merely recomputing an arbitrary finite value. The statement does not purport to settle convergence for general f.
